Study report · Local-MCQ-Gen v1

A benchmark of eight open-weight models writing dermatology board items.

1,920 generations. Two independent judges. One blueprint. Compiled from the dual-judge evaluation of the text-only canonical prompt, with inter-rater agreement and per-item disagreement triage.

Compiled
21 April 2026 · 18:24 UTC
Corpus
1920 items · 8 generators · 2 judges · 1,908 paired scores

Findings

The top-of-field is stable across judges: Gemma 4 31B-it tops both leaderboards with 0 % fatal-flaw items and effectively every generation scored at or near the ready-to-use threshold. Its MoE sibling Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it is within two score points at roughly one-fifth the active parameters. Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B rounds out the podium. The top-three ordering is judge-robust.

Two pre-registered hypotheses fail under both judges. Medical fine-tuning — represented here by MedGemma 27B — yields clinically plausible stems but breaks single-best-answer integrity, with fatal-flaw rates between 18 % and 53 % depending on judge. Reasoning-distilled models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Phi-4-reasoning) rank bottom-third under both judges; their chain-of-thought style frequently contradicts the keyed answer in the explanation field.

Judges agree on perfect and broken items, and disagree on the middle tier. Pearson r = 0.68 on the weighted score; Cohen's κ = 0.46 on binary ready-to-use classification. Fifty items at highest inter-judge delta are queued for board-certified review.

Dual-judge headline

  1. Both judges rank Gemma 4 31B first. 0 % fatal flaws, mean 99/100 on Qwen-Claude, 98.9/100 on Gemma-26B.
  2. Neither medical nor reasoning post-training helped. MedGemma & the R1-distill each produce 3–15x the fatal-flaw rate of the top Gemma-4 generators.
  3. Inter-judge agreement is moderate-to-strong. r = 0.68, ICC(2,1) = 0.65, κ = 0.46.
  4. 50 items queued for human adjudication where the two judges disagreed most.
01

At a glance

Every item was independently scored by two judges on the full 10-criterion blinded rubric. Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it produced zero judgment failures; the Qwen-Claude judge returned twelve unrecoverable JSON decode errors, which are queued for human review.

03

How much do the judges agree?

Enough to trust the ranking, not enough to trust any single item's weighted score as ground truth. Item-level Pearson r = 0.68 on the continuous score — the judges agree on extremes and diverge on middling items. Binary agreement on ready-to-use is 82 %; on fatal-flaw, 83 %.

04

The two outcomes that matter most.

Fatal flaws and accuracy-safe usable rate are the decision-relevant metrics. Fatal flaws are disqualifying (wrong key, multi-best-answer, insufficient stem, unsafe teaching). Accuracy-safe usable requires: no fatal flaw, accuracy_key_correctness ≥ 3, and weighted ≥ 70.

07

How we ran this.

The corpus was generated on Apple Silicon Metal (via LM Studio, Ollama, and llama.cpp) and on an RTX 5090 over Tailscale (for the Gemma-4 family, where dense-31B thinking-mode latency on Metal was ~18 minutes per item). All 1,920 items passed schema validation after at most one standardized repair pass.

Judging ran on the RTX 5090 serving Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and later Qwen-3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled, each at max_tokens=4096–7000 with a strict JSON-schema-enforced response format. Judges were blinded: generator model, backend, seed, and quantization were stripped from the payload before each request.

Protocol deviations (fifteen in total, from pilot dual-profile-skipped through the dual-judge design) are in study/protocol_deviations.md. Reproduction steps are in study/reports/reproducibility_runbook.md.

Judges

  1. Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it · Q4_K_M. RTX 5090 via llama.cpp. Same-family with respect to the two Gemma-4 generators (flagged internally).
  2. Qwen 3.5 27B Claude-4.6-Opus distill · Q4_K_M. Cross-family vs every generator. The only near-miss is Qwen3.6-vs-Qwen3.5, treated as separate generations.

Why dual-judge

A mid-study judge swap was converted into a designed fully-crossed experiment. Every item now has independent scores from two judges, enabling Cohen's κ on binary outcomes, ICC(2,1) on the continuous score, and a principled disagreement triage for human review.

Compiled from the full study workspace at study/. Dashboard built deterministically by scripts/build_dashboard.py from study/judging/*.jsonl and study/analysis/dual_judge_*.csv.
